expected_title: Katie A. Guiton, temporary employee in the Bureau of Pensions,made eligiblefor appointment as clerk in the classifiedservice without examination. 1923 CSR 158.
page_text:
158 FORTIETH REPORT U. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. 
June 20, 1923. 
Mr. Philip R. Peelor may be appointed to a clerical position in the Postal Service at New York, N. Y., without regard to the civil service requirements. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Postmaster General. 
June 20, 1923. 
Mise Katie A. Guiton may be appointed to a clerical position in the classified service without examination, This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Interior, who states that Miss Guiton has served as translator for the Government in Cuba and has been about 10 years in the Government service, occupying a temporary clerk position in the Bureau of Pensions. The recommendation of the Secretary of the Interior is favorably indorsed by the Commissioner of Pensions, under whom Miss Guiton is serving. The Civil Service Commission did not concur in recommending the issuance of this order. 
June 20, 1923. 
In consideration of the long, faithful, and meritorious service of Lawrence Fortune, employed for more than 20 years in ‘the Bureau of Supplies and Accounts, Navy Department, who died January 25, 1923, his widow, Mrs. Nellye C. Fortune, may be appointed as clerk at $1,000 per annum in the Bureau of Supplies and Accounts, Navy Department, without regard to the civil service rules or regulations. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation of the Acting Secretary of the Navy for this order. 
June 20, 1923. 
Mrs. Lottie M. Ballard may be appointed to the position of printer’s assistant in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without regard to the civil service rules. This order was recommended by the Secretary of the Treasury in view of the facts presented to him by the director of the bureau. Mrs. Ballard served from August 8, 1918, to April 23, 1919, and from August 30, 1920, to January 3, 1921, as a printer’s assistant, having been appointed under the- Executive order of January 15, 1918, which permitted appointments in the bureau without regard to examination. She also served temporarily from January 3, 1923, to March 6, 1923, under section 4 of Civil Service Rule VIII. This service gave her no status for reinstatement under the civil service rules. Her husband, who was confined on May 23 in the Government Hospital for the Insane, leaving her without support for herself and a young child, served for about five years as a skilled helper 
at $3 per diem in the bureau. The Civil Service Commission]did not concur in recommending this order.

EXECUTIVE ORDERS 
GENERAL ORDERS AMENDING THE CIVIL-SERVICE RULES 
RETRANSFER UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS OF PERSONS WHO LEFT THE CLASSI￾FIED SERVICE TO ENTER THE SERVICE OF A STATE, COUNTY, MUNICIPALITY, 
OR FOREIGN GOVERNMENT 
May 2, 1924 
Civil Service Rule X, section 3, is hereby amended to allow retransfer under certain conditions of persons who left the classified service to ‘enter the service of a State, county, municipality, or foreign government. As amended the section will read as follows: “SeEctioN 3. Any person may be retransferred to a position in which he was formerly employed or to any position to which transfer could be made therefrom if since his transfer he has served continuously and satisfactorily under any of the following conditions: “(1) In the executive or judicial civil service of the United States or of its insular possessions. : “(2) In the legislative service if he entered the classified service upon com- petitive WRB and the legislative service by transfer thereform. “(3) In the service of a State, county, municipality, or foreign government in a position in which he has acquired valuable training and experience.” Such retransfer may be made without compliance with clauses (b), (¢), (d), and (e) of section 8 of this rule. 
REVOCATION OF PROVISIONS IN THE CIVIL-SERVICE RULES GOVERNING TRANSFERS 
IN EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENTS AND INDEPENDENT ESTABLISHMENTS IN ACCORD￾ANCE WITH THE CLASSIFICATION ACT OF MARCH 4, 1923 
June 19, 1924 
The provisions of the acts of June 22, 1906, and October 6, 1917, which require an employee to have served for a term of three years in an executive department or independent establishment at Washington, D. C., before transfer to another department or establishment, having been repealed by the classification act of March 4, 1923, the similar provision in the civil-service rules governing transfer is hereby revoked. Employees will be permitted to remain in the positions to which they have been allocated in accordance with the classification aet of 1923 and receive the compensation attaching to such allocations, although contrary to existing provi- sions of the civil-service rules, but shall not thereby be given any different status for promotion or transfer than they had acquired under the civil-service rules prior to such allocation. 
TIME LIMITATION OF FIVE YEARS ON REINSTATEMENT OF THOSE ELIGIBLE BY REASON OF MILITARY SERVICE REMOVED BY AMENDING CLAUSE (b) 
AND REVOKING CLAUSES (¢) AND (d) OF REINSTATEMENT RULE IX 
June 19, 1924 
The time limitation of five years on reinstatement of those eligible by reason of military service is hereby removed by amending clause (b) of Reinstatement Rule IX to read as follows, and by revoking clauses (¢) and (d) of said rule: “(b) A person honorably released from the active military or naval service of the United States after service in the Civil War, or the war with Spain, or the war with Germany, or his widow, or an Army nurse of any of said wars may be reinstated within five years from the date of separation. When the com- mission and the appointing officer are in agreement that the public interest 
rey ires such action reinstatement may be made without time limit.” lauses (¢) and (d) are hereby revoked and clauses (¢) and (f) are relettered 
(¢) and (d), respectively. 
103
next_page_text:
104 FORTY-FIRST REPORT U. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION 
As amended Rule IX will read as follows: 
“1. A person separated without delinquency or misconduct from a com- petitive position or from a position which he entered by transfer or promotion from a competitive position or to accept another appointment in the executive civil service may be reinstated upon certificate of the commission subject to the following limitations: : 
““(a) Unless otherwise provided hereinafter, a person may be reinstated only to the department or independent Government establishment from which separated and upon requisition made within one year from the date of his separation. When the commission and the appointing officer are in agree- ment that the public interest requires such unusual action, the commission may allow reinstatement in any part of the classified service, and it may also author- ize waiver of the one-year limit herein prescribed under the following time limitations: Two years where service has been two years but less than ‘three years; three years where service has been three years but less than four years; four years where service has been four years but less than five years; 
and five years where service has been five years or more. ““(b) A person honorably released from the active military or naval service 
of the United States after service in the Civil War, or the war with Spain, or the war with Germany, or his widow, or an Army nurse of any of said wars may be reinstated within five years from the date of separation. When the commission and the appointing officer are in agreement that the public interest requires such action reinstatement may be made without time limit. “(¢) A former classified employee retired upon annuity under the act of May 22, 1920, by reason of total disability, who is eligible for reinstatement in his 
former department or office by reason of recovery and termination of annuity, shall also be eligible for reinstatement to an appropriate position in any part of the service, subject to the conditions and limitations of the civil-service rules. “(d) No person in any of the foregoing groups may be reinstated to a position requiring an examination different from that required in the position from which he was separated without passing an appropriate examination.”

FOREMEN ENGAGED UPON ROAD AND TRAIL CONSTRUCTION, AND TELEPHONE 
OPERATORS, TEMPORARILY EMPLOYED, FOREST SERVICE, DEPARTMENT OF

expected_title: Bess Vivian Dietrich made eligiblefor employment as messenger in the Navy Dept. without regard to Civil Service Rules. 1924 CSR 112.
page_text:
112 FORTY-FIRST REPORT U. S. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION 
June 27, 1924 ; 
Jerry Sullivan may be appointed guard in the United States Penitentiary, Leavenworth, without reference to the requirements of the civil-service rules. Mr. Sullivan was appointed to this position by the Attorney General on July 14, 1897, prior to the date on which the first examination for the position of guard was held, and he has served continuously in that position ever since. This action is based upon the recommendation of the Attorney General, who states that there is an abundance of testimony to the effect that Mr. Sullivan is a very efficient, capable guard, and there is unanimity of opinion among those who are familiar with the case that he should enjoy a civil-service status. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation. For the good of the service and justice to a veteran employee. 
June 27, 1924 
In consideration of the faithful, meritorious, and valuable services of Boat- swain Arthur Dietrich, who was killed in line of duty at the U. S. Naval Air Station, Anacostia, D. C., on March 3, 1924, after serving in the Navy contin- uously since October 6, 1909, his widow, Mrs. Bessie Vivian Dietrich, may be employed as messenger under the Navy Department without regard to the civil service act or rules. This action is recommended by the Secretary of the Navy. The Civil Service Commission does not concur in this recommendation. Issued for charity. 
July 17, 1924 
Mr. Frederick J. Crocker may be reinstated in his former position of chief of the stamp gumming division of the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, from which he was dismissed on March 31, 1922. Mr. Crocker has been thus far pre- cluded from reinstatement by the fact that he was granted an annuity as a me- chanic retirable at 65, which action, it appears from a review of the case, was based on misleading information, his proper retirement age being 70. The Treasury Department, the Department of the Interior, and the Civil Service Commission are in agreement upon this action. 
August 6, 1924 
Mrs. Cora M. Goldsworthy may be appointed to a position in the Treasury Department without compliance with the civil-service rules. Mrs. Goldsworthy is the widow of Benjamin Goldsworthy, who died in June, 1923, after a service of 17 years in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing. POSITIONS IN THE UNITED STATES VETERANS' BUREAU EXCEPTED FROM EXAMINA￾TION
October 29, 1924.
Schedule A of classified positions excepted from examination under Rule II,
section 3, is hereby amended by the addition of the following:
"XVIII. U. S. VETERANS' BUREAU
"1. Six assistant directors.
"2. One medical director.
"3. One general counsel.
"4. One assistant to the director.
"5. Chairman, central board of appeals.
"6. Fourteen area control officers.
"7. Any local physician employed on a fee basis or a part-time basis, where,
in the opinion of the commission, the establishment of registers is impracticable.
"8. Professional or technical specialists when employed temporarily for con￾sultation purposes."
This order is issued upon the joint recommendation of the United States
Veterans' Bureau and the Civil Service Commission.
RETIRED ENLISTED MEN AND RETIRED POLICEMEN AND FIREMEN EXCEPTED FROM
EXAMINATION FOR GUARD
March 9, 1925.
Schedule A of positions excepted from the requirement of examination under
the civil service rules is hereby amended by the addition of a new subdivision to
read as follows:
XIX. OFFICE OF PUBLIC BUILDINGS AND PUBLIC PARKS OF THE NATIONAL CAPITAL
"Retired enlisted men who have served in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps,
or Coast Guard, retired policemen and firemen of the District of Columbia,
and retired United States park policemen may be appointed as guards when, in
the opinion of the Commission, it is not expedient to make appointments from
competitive examination."
The above draft is concurred in by the Secretary of War, the Secretary of
Navy, the Director of Public Buildings and Public Parks of the National Capital,
and the Civil Service Commission.

March 13, 1925.
Schedule A, Subdivision III, section 1, positions excepted from examination
under the civil service rules, which reads as follows:
"1. One confidential clerk, if authorized by the Secretary of the Treasury, to
each of the following officers:
"The collector of each customs district where the receipts for the last
preceding fiscal year amounted to as much as $500,000.

March 24, 1925.

of three additional assistants to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary of
Commerce. The paragraph as amended will read as follows:
"6. Four assistants to the Secretary in the Office of the Secretary of Commerce."

who states that the positions involve duties which are peculiarly personal and
confidential, and are similar to the position of Assistant to the Secretary of the
Interior which was placed under paragraph 25, Subdivision VIII, of Schedule A
by the order of April 21, 1911, and are similar generally to the position of private
secretary or confidential clerk provided in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Subdivision I of
Schedule A. The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur in the recom￾mendation for the exception of these positions from examination.
PRESERVATION OF THE RIGHTS OF VILLAGE CARRIERS IN POST OFFICES UPON THE
RELEGATION OF THE OFFICES BELOW THE SECOND CLASS
March 25, 1925.
Section 3, Subdivision VII, Schedule A, which provides:
"All employees on star routes and in post offices of the third and fourth
classes, other than postmasters of the fourth class, except those in Alaska,
Guam, Hawaii, Porto Rico, and Samoa,"
is amended to read as follows:
"3. All employees on star routes and in post offices of the third and fourth
classes except village delivery carriers who were regularly employed in a
first or second class post office upon the relegation of the office below the
second class and postmasters of the fourth class other than those in Alaska,
Guam, Hawaii, Porto Rico, and Samoa."
The amendment preserves the rights of village carriers in post offices upon the
relegation of the offices below the second class.
This order is recommended by the Civil Service Commission with the con￾currence of the Postmaster General.

Mrs. Sullivan served in the bureau from June 9, 1908, until July 21, 1917,
when she resigned to be married. She is the widow of Charles A. Sullivan, a

March 10, 1925.
Mrs. Olive B. Robinson, who has been satisfactorily serving temporarily in the
Washington General Intermediate Depot, may be appointed to a clerkship in
the War Department without reference to the civil-service rules. This action is
recommended by the Secretary of War. The Civil Service Commission does not
concur.
Done for charity.
March 10, 1925.
Mrs. Catherine Griffin may be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau of
Engraving and Printing without regard to the length of time she has been sepa￾rated from the service.
This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury,
who states that Mrs. Griffin is the wife of Peter J. Griffin, who incurred disability
in the line of duty while fighting in the War with Germany and who is unable to
earn enough to support himself, his wife, and a 4-year-old child. The Civil
Service Commission concurs in recommending this order.
March 14, 1925.
Mrs. Virginia R. Guilfoyle, who served three years as yeoman (F) in the Naval
Reserve Force during the war and who was very seriously injured in an auto￾mobile accident in 1923 in which her husband, a member of an Army Reserve
Unit, was killed, leaving her with two small children dependent upon her for sup￾port, may be appointed to any clerical position under the Navy Department
which she is qualified to fill, without regard to civil service rules or regulations.
This action is recommended by the Secretary of the Navy. The Civil Service
Commission does not concur.
Done for charity.
March 16, 1925.
Mr. Albert B. Nichols may be reinstated in the classified service of the Treas￾ury Department without regard to the length of time he has been separated
from the service.
This order is issued on the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury,
who states that it is desired to assign Mr. Nichols to the work of designing and
constructing the customs buildings in Porto Rico, for which work he is eminently
fitted by training and experience. The Civil Service Commission concurs in
recommending this order.
March 20, 1925.
Mrs. Louise M. Linthicum whose name appears on the calculating machine
operator register with a rating of 90.85 but is not within reach for certification
may be appointed in the classified service without regard to her standing on the
register. Mrs. Linthicum has been serving under temporary appointment as a
comptometer operator since June 24, 1924. The Civil Service Commission is
unable to concur in the issuance of this order.
Done for charity.
March 31, 1925.
Mrs. C. W. Salter may be appointed keeper of the Turkey Point Light Station
without reference to the provisions of the civil service rules. Mrs Salter is left
with three children without means of support by the death of her husband,
Clarence W. Salter, for many years a keeper in the Lighthouse Service. This
order is issued upon the recommendation of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce.
The Civil Service Commission submits the order without prejudice but is without
authority to recommend its issuance.
Done for charity.

EXECUTIVE ORDERS 119
April 3, 1925. 
Mrs. Anna T. Gibson may be appointed to a clerkship in the post office at
New York City without regard to the requirements of the civil service rules.
Mrs. Gibson is the widow of William A. Gibson, for 37 years a faithful employee
of the New York City post office who, at his death, left her with one dependent
child. This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Postmaster General.
The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur.
Done for charity.
April 6, 1925. 
Mr. Roy A. Finney may be appointed in any department, establishment, or
office in the classified service of the United States, in any position for which his
qualifications fit him, and where there is need of his services, witliout reference
to the requirements of the civil service rules.
Mr. Finney is an honorably discharged sailor from the United States Navy,
where he served two enlistments. Following his discharge from the naval service
he was injured while employed in private industry. He passed the examination
for post-office clerk at Newark, N. J., on July 31, 1920, with an average of 80.30.
His physical condition necessitated cancellation of his eligibility.
Mr. Finney has endeavored to pass examinations for the departmental service
where physical disability is not a bar, and was a competitor in six such examina￾tions. The Civil Service Commission does not recommend this order.
Done for charity.
May 2, 1925. 
Mrs. Bessie L. Dudley may be appointed in the classified service of the Treas￾ury Department without regard to her standing on the eligible register. This
order is issued upon the recommendation of the Secretary of the Treasury, who
states that she is the daughter of a former officer in the United States Revenue
Cutter Service and a widow with a family of small children to support.
The Civil Service Commission submits the order without prejudice but is
without authority to recommend its issuance.
Done for charity.
June 4, 1925.
